codeReview.summary: Fix review for fnd-fix-db-backend-app-and-docs-compliance (commit d835bc9e, worker 4d991f66, backend-worker skill; skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true, no deviations). I re-read the worker's transcript skeleton and all three diffs (bc4326f7 migrations, 452bb463 auth/routing/guards/seed, d835bc9e fix) and adjudicated the 8 prior blocking findings one by one against the CURRENT tree. All 8 are RESOLVED in code and tests, and the non-blocking rsv_holds_single_conversion tightening is present. The one unmet piece is machine state, not code: the KSA local tenant DB that services.yaml actually starts for tenant-api-ksa still carries the pre-fix trigger definitions (the two US-dir DBs were refreshed by hand with the new trigger SQL, the KSA dir copy was not), so the fix's own expectedBehavior clause 'workers/migrations.generated.ts and seeded local US/KSA tenant DBs are in sync' is only 2/3 true and the local KSA data plane still enforces the old, contract-violating semantics. Everything else in the fix is correct and covered: trigger predicates and abort string, the 409 mapping through a real SQLite trigger abort, the DO-bundle auto-generation in the tenant-db test, the context cache parameters, the hasProvisionedDb refusals on operator/public/internal surfaces, the expanded per-route security sweeps, the single-location picker gate, and the canonical docs vocabulary. Newly written docs text does contain factual drift about trigger names/messages and implied-read rules (non-blocking; VAL-FND-024's bar is the 8 permissions plus 6 flags, which are now correct).

issues.description: The fix left the KSA local tenant DB with the pre-fix triggers, so the original finding-1/finding-2 defect is still live on the KSA local data plane and the feature's stated outcome ('workers/migrations.generated.ts and seeded local US/KSA tenant DBs are in sync') is only partially met. Evidence (read-only sqlite3 SELECT on sqlite_master): packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db still defines rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert / _update as `RAISE(ABORT, 'table_overlap')` with an EXISTS filter of only `o.active = 1` (no `o.overbook = 0`), and rsv_holds_single_conversion as `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted' AND NEW.status = 'converted'`; the refreshed copies packages/database/db/tenant_t58bgatqh3rv0s3movrecyj1.db (acme) and packages/database/db/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db (same org, US dir) both carry the new 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap' string, `o.overbook = 0` and `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted'`. This is the exact directory used by the local KSA node: services.yaml `tenant-api-ksa.start` sets TENANT_DB_DIR=/home/factory-user/repos/menuza/packages/database/db/ksa, and environment.md:74 documents it as the tenant-api KSA database. Concrete failure path: with the KSA node running, an INSERT/UPDATE of a normal (active = 1, overbook = 0) occupancy that overlaps an existing staff overbook row still aborts with 'table_overlap' on the KSA side instead of succeeding as VAL-FND-011 requires, and the tightened hold rule does not apply there either. The DB cannot self-heal: __drizzle_migrations already records 0016 as applied (17 rows, last created_at 2026-10-15 23:59:54), and mission AGENTS.md forbids deleting tenant DB files, so both seed_reservations_ksa and tenant-api startup leave the old trigger SQL in place. Mitigating context for triage: no validation-contract tool reads this artifact (VAL-FND-011/012 run packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts against a freshly-migrated temp DB), so this is a machine-state sync fix (drop/recreate the three triggers in that file with the new SQL, or rebuild the KSA tenant DB through provisioning), not a product-code change.

ADR 048 section 5 (lines 167-176) and docs/reservations-plan.md:27-33 document triggers and abort strings that do not exist in 0016_reservations_foundation.sql, and this fix is what wrote the specific identifiers. 0016 defines exactly 9 triggers (verified by grep: rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert/_update, rsv_holds_single_conversion, rsv_reservation_events_no_delete/_no_update, rsv_audit_log_no_delete/_no_update, rsv_guest_merges_no_delete/_no_update) - there is no `rsv_holds_no_overlap_insert`/`rsv_holds_no_overlap_update` and no artifact anywhere raises 'rsv_reservation_holds overlap' (hold conflicts are carried by the rsv_table_occupancies triggers, kind='hold' rows). The event triggers are named rsv_reservation_events_no_update/_no_delete (not `rsv_events_no_update`/`rsv_events_no_delete`), they raise 'append_only' (0016:838,848) not 'rsv_reservation_events is append-only', and the only permitted redaction is `NEW.data = '{"redacted":true}'` (0016:842) - the ADR says `NEW.payload IS NULL` and reservations-plan.md:37-38 additionally claims mapSqliteConstraintError maps 'rsv_reservation_holds overlap' to 409, which it does not (apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:580-582 maps only 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap', 'hold_already_converted', 'uniq_rsv_reservations_hold_id'). VAL-FND-024's bar (contract:151-157) is coverage of the ADR topics plus the permissions/flags listing, which are satisfied, so this is documentation accuracy rather than a gate failure; the risk is that later milestones copy non-existent trigger names from the canonical ADR.

The implied-read prose this fix wrote does not match the implementation. docs/permissions.md:212-216 (and the same list in ADR 048:211-215) says `update:reservation_guest:any` implies `read:reservation_guest:any` **and `read:reservation:any`** - the code maps guest to read_reservation_guest only (apps/app/app/utils/organization/tenant-role-permissions.ts:105-107 and packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts:59-61; asserted by app/utils/organization/tenant-role-permissions.test.ts:152-159), and omits that `update:reservation_payment:any` also implies `read:reservation_report:any` (tenant-role-permissions.ts:108-111, test lines 160-168). The 8 permission strings themselves (permissions.md:198-205) and the 6 flags plus reservations.platform_fee_bp (permissions.md:256-262) are exactly right, so the VAL-FND-024 requirement is met; only the extra prose is wrong.

Residual docs/verification drift in the same touched files, for the orchestrator to fold into a docs pass: (a) ADR 048:44 and docs/reservations-plan.md:22 still say 'All 24 rsv_* tables' / '24 `rsv_*` tables' while the implemented schema is 41 tables (0016 has 41 CREATE TABLE statements; reservations-schema.test.ts:106 asserts ALL_RSV_TABLES.length === 41), and ADR section 1 lists non-existent names (rsv_reservation_holds, rsv_table_blocks, rsv_payment_records, rsv_slot_overrides, rsv_date_overrides) where the code has rsv_holds, rsv_blocks, rsv_payments, rsv_special_days; (b) ADR 048:215 says four role presets where packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts:133-192 defines seven (the four required sets are exact, the rest additive); (c) ADR 048:255-262 describes erase-customer nulling reservation/hold/waitlist rows and event payloads, while the shipped route (apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-internal.ts:100-115) only scrubs the rsv_guests row (foundation scaffold; the column is `data`, not `payload`). None of these are in the 8 adjudicated findings and none break a contract tool, but they are in files this feature was asked to bring in line with the code.

The 3 s upstream timeout is implemented but not asserted. reservations-context.ts:53 sets `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(3_000)` and the test asserts the fresh/stale/cooldown constants and `redirect: 'error'` via expect.objectContaining({ redirect, headers }) (reservations-context.test.ts:108-134) without checking `signal`; a future edit could drop the timeout and the suite would stay green. VAL-FND-018's cache parameters are otherwise verified (constants at lines 109-111, stale/cooldown behaviour at 144-187), so this is a small coverage gap, not a defect.

sharedStateObservations.observation: library/environment.md has no gotcha for the trap this fix hit: editing a hand-appended SQL block (triggers) inside an already-committed tenant migration does NOT reach existing local tenant DBs, because __drizzle_migrations records the file as applied and tenant DB files must not be deleted, and there are TWO local tenant DB roots to refresh (packages/database/db for the US node and packages/database/db/ksa for the KSA node started by services.yaml tenant-api-ksa). Add a gotcha plus the sqlite3 refresh recipe (DROP/CREATE the changed triggers in each tenant_*.db under both directories, then verify with `SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='trigger'`).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db still has 'table_overlap'/no-overbook triggers while packages/database/db/tenant_*.db copies were refreshed; both ledgers show 0016 already applied (__drizzle_migrations count 17, max created_at 2026-10-15 23:59:54); library/environment.md:66-79 lists the DB locations but not this consequence; mission AGENTS.md forbids deleting tenant DB files.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Two library/staffing-patterns.md statements are now stale after d835bc9e and should be updated so later workers are not misled: line 48 still says the repo docs 'currently describe an older vocabulary' for reservations (the fix reconciled docs/permissions.md, docs/reservations-contract.md, docs/reservations-plan.md and ADR 048), and line 85 still says a test reading apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts fails on a clean checkout (reservations-schema.test.ts:141-149 now runs apps/tenant-api/scripts/generate-do-migrations.mjs when the file is absent).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: library/staffing-patterns.md:48 and :85 vs docs/permissions.md:198-205/256-262, docs/reservations-contract.md:15-54, packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts:141-149, handoff verification `rm -f apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts && npm test -w @repo/tenant-db` exit 0.

sharedStateObservations.observation: skills/backend-worker/SKILL.md:25 already lists the full security-sweep contract (both wrong audiences, over-long TTL, impersonated-write, cross-org, excluded locationIds, unprovisioned org 404) and the worker followed it (handoff followedProcedure=true, no deviations), so the round-1 skill guidance landed. The remaining skill gap is the same as the knowledge gap above: there is no step telling a worker that after editing SQL/triggers inside an already-committed migration they must also refresh every existing local tenant DB (both TENANT_DB_DIR roots) or explicitly state which DBs were refreshed and which were not in the handoff ('updated local tenant DB triggers' in this handoff was true for the US dirs only).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: skills/backend-worker/SKILL.md:25; handoff.whatWasImplemented ('updated local tenant DB triggers'); handoff.verification (only US-dir suites + browser checks on acme/riyadh-grill via the App, no KSA node DB check); sqlite_master of packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission AGENTS.md says 'Never edit a migration an earlier feature committed; add a new one', but this fix's approved description required editing 0016 in place - and an in-place edit is precisely what cannot re-apply to already-provisioned/seed DBs. Either add the refresh procedure (knowledge/skill items above) or record the exception explicitly in AGENTS.md so the rule and the approved fix do not contradict each other.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: mission AGENTS.md 'Migrations' bullet; fnd-fix-db-backend-app-and-docs-compliance.description item (1) instructing the 0016 edit; git show d835bc9e -- packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql (8 changed lines in an already-committed migration).

sharedStateObservations.observation: services.yaml has no command that makes an existing local tenant DB match its migration SQL (commands.seed_reservations_acme/seed_reservations_ksa are no-ops for already-applied migrations), so any future in-place trigger/migration correction will hit the same KSA/US split with no approved tool to fix it. Consider a `refresh_tenant_triggers` helper (read-only-verify + DROP/CREATE for the changed triggers, run for both TENANT_DB_DIR roots) or an explicit note in the seed commands.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: services.yaml commands.seed_reservations_acme / seed_reservations_ksa and services.tenant-api-ksa.start (TENANT_DB_DIR=packages/database/db/ksa); packages/tenant-db/src/migrations.ts applies only journal entries newer than the ledger; KSA DB sqlite_master still holds the pre-fix trigger SQL.

summary: FIX REVIEW of fnd-fix-db-backend-app-and-docs-compliance (worker 4d991f66, commit d835bc9e on top of bc4326f7 + 452bb463), adjudicating the 8 round-1 blocking findings against the current tree. All 8 are RESOLVED; one machine-state item is NOT RESOLVED, so the fix feature is marked fail on that single point. (1) 'Occupancy overlap triggers omitted the required `o.overbook = 0` predicate (staff overbook rows must not block normal occupancies)' -> RESOLVED: packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql:811 and :826 now include `AND o.overbook = 0` in both EXISTS clauses, and packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts:1242-1268 inserts and updates a normal (active=1, overbook=0) occupancy that overlaps an overbook=1 row and asserts success. (2) 'Trigger abort message was `table_overlap`, not the contract's `rsv_table_occupancies overlap`; mapSqliteConstraintError did not map it to 409' -> RESOLVED: both RAISE calls now emit 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap' (0016:806, :820), the schema test asserts that string (1187, 1220, 1289), apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:574-584 matches message+cause and throws the 409 conflict, and reservations-write.test.ts:328-393 drives a real trigger abort through withReservationWrite and asserts { status: 409, code: 'conflict' }; apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts on disk was regenerated (contains the new string and predicate). (3) 'Tenant-db schema test read a gitignored artifact with no generator in its task graph' -> RESOLVED: reservations-schema.test.ts:141-149 runs apps/tenant-api/scripts/generate-do-migrations.mjs via execFileSync when the file is absent; the generator only reads the drizzle journal/SQL, so a clean checkout works (handoff: rm + `npm test -w @repo/tenant-db` exit 0, 13 files/177 tests). (4) 'Reservations context cache used 60 s/5 min with no failure cooldown' -> RESOLVED: apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-context.ts:10-12 sets 300_000/86_400_000/30_000, :24-27 adds the failure LRU, :94-103 the cooldown, :52-53 keep redirect:'error' and AbortSignal.timeout(3_000); reservations-context.test.ts:109-111 and 144-187 pin the constants, stale window and cooldown (the 3 s timeout itself is not asserted - non-blocking note). (5) 'No hasProvisionedDb check on reservations paths' -> RESOLVED: reservations-operator.ts:30-37, reservations-public.ts:48-53 and reservations-internal.ts:51-54 all return uniform 404 { error: 'not_found' } for active-but-unprovisioned orgs, and the security sweep asserts it per route (reservations-security.test.ts:409-430; fixture ORG_UNPROVISIONED at :243-250); ADR 048:120-122 and docs/reservations-contract.md:50-54 now document it. (6) 'Security sweep omitted tenant-api-operator audience, over-long TTL and impersonated-write variants' -> RESOLVED: both wrong audiences (reservations-security.test.ts:284-289), three over-long-TTL variants (293-312), impersonated-write on every non-GET route (385-407), and cross-org ORG_B plus excluded locationIds on every mounted route (432-505) are now swept; the sweep also asserts never-5xx. (7) 'Location picker never hidden for a single-location organization' -> RESOLVED: apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/_layout.tsx:183 renders the selector only when locations.length > 1 (child sections still resolve a location because selectedLocationId falls back to locations[0]?.id at :82-83), with a static guard test (reservations-guards.test.ts:92) and the handoff's browser check on riyadh-grill. (8) 'Docs list a permission/claim/audience vocabulary that does not exist in code' -> RESOLVED: docs/permissions.md:198-205 lists the 8 exact permission strings and :256-262 the 6 reservations.* flags (plus platform_fee_bp), migration 0025 at :190; docs/reservations-contract.md:13-36 carries aud 'tenant-api-reservations-operator', the orgId/region/scope/grants/locationIds/features/impersonated claims and TTL caps, :40-46 Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN>; ADR 048 now has all 12 decision sections (headings 42-266) including payments split, voice boundary, messaging/tick, erasure and kill switches; docs/reservations.md:54 updated. The non-blocking one-line tightening is present: rsv_holds_single_conversion is `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted'` (0016:831-836) with tests for re-conversion and for flipping a converted hold to another status (reservations-schema.test.ts:1331-1347); no code path updates converted holds (the sweep filters status='active', reservations-write.ts:177-183), so no regression. Guard additions (reservations-guard.ts:80-97) add orgId/X-Org-Id mismatch 403 and location checks before handlers; no App caller sends those (grep: X-Org-Id appears only in the security test) and the only :locationId route already ran requireReservationsLocation, so no regression. THE ONE UNRESOLVED ITEM: the KSA local tenant DB used by the KSA node (packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db, per services.yaml tenant-api-ksa TENANT_DB_DIR) still contains the pre-fix triggers - 'table_overlap', no `o.overbook = 0`, and `WHEN OLD.status='converted' AND NEW.status='converted'` - while the two US-dir DBs (acme and the same org) were refreshed. Because __drizzle_migrations already records 0016 as applied and mission rules forbid deleting tenant DB files, re-seeding does not fix it, so the fix's expectedBehavior clause 'workers/migrations.generated.ts and seeded local US/KSA tenant DBs are in sync' is only partially met and the round-1 trigger defect remains observable on the local KSA data plane. No contract tool depends on that artifact (VAL-FND-011/012 use the schema test on a fresh temp DB), so the remedy is a small machine-state refresh (DROP/CREATE the three triggers in that file with the new SQL) rather than a code change. Docs written by this fix also contain non-blocking inaccuracies (non-existent holds-overlap/event trigger names and abort strings in ADR 048 section 5 and docs/reservations-plan.md; '24 rsv_* tables' vs the implemented 41; two wrong implied-read rules; four role presets vs seven; erase-customer scope), all listed as non-blocking issues with file:line evidence.
